workspace: uncommitted certificate boundary and snapshot evidence after 0.4.2
intent: Prior recovery authority design entry in the probe ledger
source_findings: The System API version changes for ordinary execution and management and may increase arbitrarily
Atomicity is scoped to a single message; an inter-canister await separates executions
Snapshot loading requires controller authority and replaces code and memory
Management history is bounded and cannot supply complete blob or funding inventory
The current core requires a synchronous whole certificate handler and relies on host-owned recovery qualification
The current standalone host deliberately supplies recovery_ready=false
design_inferences: A cached witness permit can be part of a rolled-back heap; it is insufficient as the recovery mechanism
An external watermark alone cannot reconstruct the missing economic and identity records
Preserving storage-owner backup recovery requires complete surviving records and governance of restore/restart outside that backup
Recommended proposal: one external bounded write-ahead journal and recovery controller, with the existing service retaining provider identity and shared workflows
Certificate issuance needs a journal prelude followed by one synchronous final exposure-write/reply message
The journal is the recoverable commit point; incomplete local materialization must not serve as current state
A lasting provider owner without rollback could avoid replication only if the maintainer explicitly narrows the storage backup recovery contract
cleanup: None; no provider objects, accounts or local canister instances created
limitations: Official web sources are linked; raw HTTP responses and transport request counts were not captured
No authority implementation, controller enforcement or end-to-end recovery was tested in this review
The controller/journal itself must remain outside the service rollback domain under explicit governance trust
Metadata cost, latency, capacity and reconstruction limits require measurement
Provider pre-charge, namespace, replay charging, deletion and billing qualification remain independently open
